note: Doses are evidence-based OPTIMAL ranges for a healthy adult (not label RDIs), editable, and not medical advice. Some (e.g. vitamin D) are best guided by bloodwork. 'daily' supplements default to AM, 'sleep' to PM.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + K2 Spray
supplements.dose_note: Each spray ~1000 IU D3 + 45 mcg K2 (MK-7). 2 sprays = ~2000 IU D3 + 90 mcg K2. Take with a fat-containing meal. D3 dose is best guided by a 25-OH-vitamin-D blood level.

supplements.name: B-Complex #12
supplements.dose_note: Active-form B vitamins (methylfolate, methyl-B12). Morning with food — B vitamins can be mildly energising.

supplements.name: UltraClean DHA Omega
supplements.dose_note: 500 mg DHA + 100 mg EPA per cap. Optimal general intake ~1-2 g omega-3/day; DHA-weighted, which suits an APOE E4 profile. Take with fat for absorption.

supplements.name: Glycine
supplements.dose_note: 3 g glycine before bed is the sleep-studied dose (improves sleep quality and next-day alertness). ~1 g per serve, so ~3 serves.

supplements.name: Triple Magnesium
supplements.optimal_dose: 1 x 5 g scoop, 30-60 min before bed
supplements.dose_note: ~250-300 mg elemental magnesium (glycinate/citrate) per scoop — a strong sleep/recovery form.
supplements.caution: You also have MagZorb magnesium — don't run both at full dose. Keep total supplemental elemental magnesium ~300-400 mg/day to avoid loose stools.

supplements.name: Tongkat Ali (Long Jack)
supplements.dose_note: Optimal ~200 mg/day of a standardised extract; take in the morning (can be mildly stimulating). Note: its main draw — raising testosterone — is largely redundant while you're on TRT, but it may still help cortisol/stress, mood and libido.

supplements.name: Inositol (40:1 Myo:D-Chiro)
supplements.dose_note: Supports insulin sensitivity, mood and metabolic health — relevant to a rising fasting glucose. Also calming, so a PM dose is a fine option. Can be split.

supplements.name: L-Theanine 200mg
supplements.dose_note: Dual use: PM for calm/sleep, OR AM alongside coffee to smooth out caffeine jitters and blunt the cortisol spike — a good fit given cortisol sensitivity and a morning stimulant routine.

supplements.name: Vitamin C 1000mg
supplements.dose_note: 1000 mg with food, or split morning/evening. Well above the RDI but a common optimal antioxidant/immune dose.

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate 500mg
supplements.dose_note: ~100 mg elemental magnesium per cap (label states 100 mg per dose). Good for sleep.
supplements.caution: Counts toward your total magnesium alongside Pillar Triple Mag — keep combined elemental magnesium ~300-400 mg/day.

supplements.name: Phosphatidylserine 500mg
supplements.dose_note: Lowers cortisol — directly relevant to cortisol sensitivity — and supports sleep and stress. The label serving is 500 mg; the evidence-based optimal is ~100-300 mg, so you likely don't need a full serving. Also useful post-training.

supplements.name: Liposomal Apigenin
supplements.dose_note: Apigenin (~50 mg) is a popular sleep aid; liposomal form is more bioavailable. Stacks well with magnesium, theanine and glycine as a sleep protocol.

supplements.name: Creatine Monohydrate
supplements.dose_note: The most evidence-backed supplement for strength, muscle and cognition. Timing doesn't matter; daily consistency does.

supplements.name: Ashwagandha (KSM-66)
supplements.dose_note: Lowers cortisol and perceived stress — a strong fit given cortisol sensitivity. Evening dose is common; can also be AM.

supplements.name: Berberine
supplements.dose_note: Improves fasting glucose and lipids — relevant to a rising fasting glucose.
supplements.caution: Adds to the glucose-lowering effect of your retatrutide/tesamorelin/MOTS-c — watch for lows, especially early.

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.dose_note: Supports testosterone, immunity and skin. Don't take with coffee, calcium or iron; long-term high doses need balancing copper.

supplements.name: Taurine
supplements.dose_note: Supports cardiovascular health, exercise capacity and glucose handling.

supplements.name: Ubiquinol (CoQ10)
supplements.dose_note: Mitochondrial and cardiovascular support; take with a fatty meal.

supplements.name: Curcumin (phytosome)
supplements.dose_note: Anti-inflammatory — useful for joint/knee issues. Use a bioavailable form (phytosome or with piperine).

supplements.name: Collagen Peptides
supplements.dose_note: Supports tendon, joint and skin — complements tissue-repair goals. Pairs well with vitamin C.

supplements.name: NAC
supplements.dose_note: Glutathione precursor; antioxidant and liver support.

supplements.name: Boron
supplements.dose_note: Can raise free testosterone by lowering SHBG; also supports bone.

supplements.name: Melatonin
supplements.dose_note: Low doses (0.5-1 mg) are often as effective as higher ones for sleep onset with fewer next-day effects.

supplements.name: Electrolytes (Na/K/Mg)
supplements.dose_note: Useful on GLP-1s or lower-carb eating, where sodium/potassium can drop and cause fatigue or cramps.
